title: Capital Gains Tax Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Capital Gains Tax Calculator: Estimate US federal tax on a long-term capital gain — 2025 rates, by filing status. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it,…
content:
The [Capital Gains Tax Calculator](/capital-gains-tax-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Estimate US federal tax on a long-term capital gain — 2025 rates, by filing status. Enter your long-term capital gain, other taxable income and filing status and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Estimate the US federal tax on a long-term capital gain — profit from an asset held more than a year, such as shares or property. Long-term gains get special low rates for 2025: 0% up to $48,350 of taxable income for single filers ($96,700 married filing jointly, $64,750 head of household), then 15%, then 20% above $533,400 ($600,050 married, $566,700 head of household). Because the gain sits on top of your other income, how much of it falls in each band depends on what you already earn. This is a federal estimate only — it does not include state tax or the 3.8% net investment income tax that can apply at higher incomes — and it is not tax advice.

## How to use the Capital Gains Tax Calculator

Start by entering your long-term capital gain, then entering your other taxable income and finally choosing your filing status from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter the long-term capital gain — sale price minus what you paid, including costs.
2. Enter your other taxable income for the year.
3. Choose your filing status — the thresholds differ.
4. Read the tax, the split across the 0%, 15% and 20% bands, and the after-tax gain.

## Formula

The gain stacks on top of other taxable income. The part below the 0% threshold is untaxed, the part up to the 15% threshold is taxed at 15%, and anything above it at 20%.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Capital Gains Tax Calculator](/capital-gains-tax-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A single filer with $30,000 of other taxable income and a $50,000 long-term gain: $18,350 of the gain still fits under the $48,350 0% threshold, so it is untaxed, and the remaining $31,650 is taxed at 15% — $4,747.5 in total, a 9.5% effective rate on the gain. Try the same figures in the [Capital Gains Tax Calculator](/capital-gains-tax-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Long-term capital gain: 50000, Other taxable income: 30000, Filing status: Single), the [Capital Gains Tax Calculator](/capital-gains-tax-calculator) returns Estimated federal tax: $4,747.5, Taxed at 0%: $18,350, Taxed at 15%: $31,650, Taxed at 20%: $0, Effective rate on the gain: 9.5%, After-tax gain: $45,252.5. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Long-term vs short-term gains

Only gains on assets held more than a year get the 0/15/20% rates. Sell within a year and the gain is short-term, taxed as ordinary income at your normal bracket — up to 37%. The one-year line is the single biggest lever in capital-gains tax: holding an asset a few extra weeks can cut the tax rate by more than half.

## What this estimate leaves out

This is federal tax only. Most states tax capital gains as ordinary income on top, and single filers with modified adjusted gross income over $200,000 ($250,000 married) may owe the extra 3.8% net investment income tax. Losses from other sales can also offset gains. For a real sale, check the figure with a tax professional before you file.

## The 2025 thresholds

The 0% threshold for 2025 is $48,350 for single filers, $96,700 married filing jointly and $64,750 head of household. The 20% threshold is $533,400 single, $600,050 married and $566,700 head of household. These are the IRS figures for 2025 (Rev. Proc. 2024-40) and they move with inflation each year.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Holding an asset more than a year usually halves the tax rate or better.
- Capital losses offset capital gains — harvesting a loss can cut the tax on a gain.
- Your other income decides which band the gain falls in, so the same gain can be taxed at 0% or 20%.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the capital gains tax rate for 2025?

For long-term gains: 0% up to $48,350 of taxable income (single), 15% up to $533,400, then 20%. Married filing jointly: $96,700 and $600,050. Short-term gains are taxed as ordinary income. Try it with your own numbers in the [Capital Gains Tax Calculator](/capital-gains-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How long must I hold an asset for the long-term rate?

More than one year. Sell within a year and the gain is short-term, taxed at your ordinary income-tax rate instead of the lower capital-gains rates. Try it with your own numbers in the [Capital Gains Tax Calculator](/capital-gains-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does this include state tax?

No — this is the federal estimate only. Most states tax capital gains as ordinary income, and the 3.8% net investment income tax can apply at higher incomes. Try it with your own numbers in the [Capital Gains Tax Calculator](/capital-gains-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Capital Gains Tax Calculator use?

The gain stacks on top of other taxable income. The part below the 0% threshold is untaxed, the part up to the 15% threshold is taxed at 15%, and anything above it at 20%. You can see it in action in the [Capital Gains Tax Calculator](/capital-gains-tax-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
